‘Russia Always Calculates Its Strikes to Destroy Lives’: Zelensky Says After Deadly Overnight Attack — President Volodymyr Zelensky said 12 people, including an Indian citizen, were killed and dozens injured in Russia’s overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine. He said the strikes damaged residential and civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, the Kyiv region, Odesa, and several other regions.

Russia’s Overnight Attack Hits Romania Border Crossing, Targets Rescuers in Zaporizhzhia — Russia launched a combined overnight attack involving 218 Shahed drones and multiple missiles, mainly targeting Odesa and Kyiv regions. The strikes damaged the Orlivka crossing with Romania and targeted rescuers in Zaporizhzhia, while Ukraine reported neutralizing 199 aerial targets.

EU Frets over Kyiv’s Defences, ‘Hybrid’ Threat From Moscow — EU defense and foreign ministers will discuss strengthening Ukraine’s air defenses, new sanctions and using frozen Russian assets. They are also expected to address growing Russian hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe.

India-Russia: A Changing Equation — India-Russia relations are being reshaped by record Russian oil exports to India, growing Indian fuel shipments to Russia, persistent trade imbalances, and efforts to develop alternative transport corridors. The partnership remains resilient, but faces pressures from sanctions, Ukraine, and India’s economic priorities.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 30, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 30, 2026.

Putin Sends Support to Jailed Ex-President as Armenia Drifts From Moscow — Putin sent birthday wishes to jailed former Armenian President Robert Kocharyan ahead of a meeting with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, who holds more power than the largely ceremonial president, as Russia continues to lose its grip on Armenia.

Russia’s SCO Show Masks Shrinking Power, US Analyst Goble Says — As Putin met Xi Jinping and other leaders at the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, analyst Paul Goble told Kyiv Post that Russia is losing allies, soft power and influence, increasingly relying on other isolated states.

Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russia’s Key Baltic Oil Port of Ust-Luga — A drone attack sparked a fire at Russia’s Ust-Luga port in Leningrad region, according to Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko. The Baltic facility is a major outlet for Russian oil exports.

European Ministers Boycott Russian Counterpart After Surprise US G20 Invitation — European officials refused to pose with Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov after Washington invited him to a G20 finance meeting in Asheville, triggering backlash over Russia’s diplomatic return.

Massive Russian Missile, Drone Attack on Kyiv and Region Kills 12, Injures Over Dozen — Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing 12 people and injuring at least 18 others, including children.

Poland Opens Terrorism Probe Into Fire at Drone Factory — Polish prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation after a WB Electronics drone factory, which supplies both Kyiv and Warsaw militaries, caught fire early Monday, Aug. 31. Authorities said the blaze was deliberate and are investigating whether a foreign intelligence service was involved, though no suspects have been publicly identified.

Russian Drone Attacks Injure 9 in Kyiv Region — Russian drone attacks on the Kyiv region entered their fifth consecutive day on Monday, Aug. 31, injuring nine people and damaging infrastructure. Drone debris fell in several districts, causing fires.

Bomb Disposal Operation at Rivne Police Station Kills 1, Injures 3 — A 47-year-old police bomb technician was killed and three officers were injured in an explosion at a police department in Rivne, western Ukraine, on Monday, Aug. 31. According to Rivne region police, the State Bureau of Investigation opened a criminal case as authorities work to determine what caused the blast.

6 Wounded, Including a Child, in Russian Strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 40 times on Monday, Aug. 31, injuring six people, including a seven-year-old girl. The strikes damaged civilian infrastructure, including an apartment building and a supermarket.

Ukraine Opens 25,000 Schools Under New Wartime Safety Rules as Teachers Get Additional 20% Pay Raise — According to Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi on Monday, Aug. 31, Ukraine will open 25,000 educational institutions on Sept. 1 under new safety rules as Russia’s war continues. More than 83% of school students will now have access to shelters, while teachers’ pay will rise by an additional 20%.

Russian Drone Destroys Sorting Line at Nova Poshta's Odesa Terminal — A Russian drone strike destroyed the automated sorting line at Nova Poshta's Odesa innovation terminal overnight Aug. 30-31 – equipment the company said cannot be restored. No one was injured, and Nova Poshta switched deliveries to backup logistics schemes. It was at least the sixth reported Russian strike on the delivery operator's facilities in August alone.

Trump Envoys May Visit Ukraine as Diplomacy Remains Stalled; Russia Does Not Want Peace, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday, Aug. 31, that Ukraine and senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are discussing a possible visit to Kyiv. He said the trip could help advance stalled diplomacy, though Ukraine’s intelligence assessments indicate that Russian President Vladimir Putin still intends to continue the war.

IMF Mission Starts Work in Kyiv as Ukraine Misses Some Summer Reform Deadlines — An International Monetary Fund mission led by Gavin Gray started talks with Ukrainian officials on Aug. 31 on the economic outlook, reform commitments under the $8.1 billion Extended Fund Facility, and the 2027 draft budget.

Russian FM Lavrov Calls NATO’s Arctic Presence a Direct Threat to Russia — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Monday, Aug. 31, that NATO’s Arctic Sentry activity poses a direct security threat to Russia, accusing the alliance of militarizing the High North. His remarks came as Moscow promotes Arctic shipping and resource projects with China and India.

Ukrainian Influencer Infiltrates Russian Zoom Meeting Covering Drones, Insults Attendees — Ukrainian prankster Evhen Volnov hijacked closed Russian state video conferences on drone production and jamming systems. He confronted officials about widespread corruption, sluggish certifications, war crime complicity, and military failures before organizers abruptly cut the feeds.

Possible Sabotage Probed After Fire at Polish Drone Factory Used by Ukraine — A fire broke out overnight at a Polish defense plant producing drones and components for Ukrainian and Polish forces. Surveillance cameras reportedly captured a masked person entering the facility, while a backpack and sweatshirt were found nearby. Poland’s security services are investigating whether the blaze was an act of sabotage.

Donbasification: How Russia Manufactured an Identity — In this 2-part series, Kate Turska traces how "Donbas," once a Soviet-era economic term for a coal and steel basin, was transformed into a supposed separate identity. Drawing on decades of forced Russification and the 1991 independence referendum, she shows how genuine regional differences were exaggerated into a fault line – one Russia would later exploit to justify its 2014 invasion.

At Least 62 Ukrainians Missing in Nepal-Tibet Disaster as Death Toll Nears 1,000 — At least 61 Ukrainians remain missing after devastating floods and landslides struck Nepal and Tibet, as the disaster’s overall death toll nears 1,000. No Ukrainian deaths have been confirmed, while nearly 4,800 people remain unaccounted for across the affected areas.

‘They Will Hang Me’: Putin Fears Defeat in Ukraine, Plans to Send 400,000 More Russians to War — Russian President Vladimir Putin fears defeat in Ukraine could cost him his life and is preparing to send up to 400,000 more Russians to the battlefield, The Economist reported, citing Kremlin-linked sources. The escalation could include intensified recruitment, repression at home and expanded hybrid attacks against Ukraine’s allies.

Serbia: State Funeral For War Criminal — Ratko Mladić, the Bosnian Serb former general nicknamed the “Butcher of Bosnia”, died on Thursday in the United Nations Detention Unit in The Hague. He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in 2017 for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. Serbia’s Minister of Justice, Nenad Vujić, has announced that he will be given a state funeral - sparking a major controversy.

Ukraine's Labor Shortage Forces Firms to Rewrite Hiring Rules — Ukrainian companies are abandoning traditional hiring filters as mobilization, migration, and a growing skills mismatch make qualified workers harder to find. Vacancies that once took two to three weeks to fill now take two to three months. Wages are climbing and employers are turning to veterans, students, older workers, and automation to keep operations running.

Ukraine’s Intel Unpacks Russia’s Hypersonic ‘Zircon’ Missile – Small Warhead and Foreign Tech — Ukraine’s military intelligence has exposed new details about Russia’s costly 3M22 Zircon missile, challenging Moscow’s claims about its speed and revealing its relatively small warhead. HUR also detailed the missile’s guidance systems, construction, and the foreign equipment used by Russian companies to manufacture it.

Poland Joins US Drone-Warfare Drills Built on Ukraine’s Battlefield Lessons — Polish special forces are joining US-led drone warfare drills in Germany for the first time, training on battlefield tactics drawn from Ukraine’s war against Russia as NATO prepares for a potential confrontation with Moscow.

Kyiv Endures Unprecedented 5-Day Drone Blitz as Russia Alters Tactics — Kyiv has endured five days of relentless Russian drone attacks, with faster jet-powered UAVs, repeated air-raid alerts and deadly strikes disrupting the capital. A blast at an arms depot near Kyiv has killed 38, while two children were also among those killed in the wider barrage.

Russia’s Putin and China’s Xi to Attend Summit in Kyrgyzstan — Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping and more than a dozen other leaders will meet in Kyrgyzstan for a two-day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, bringing together Moscow’s and Beijing’s partners as the bloc seeks to expand its influence amid the wars in Ukraine and Iran, US sanctions and growing global tensions.

‘If We Need to Strike, We Will Strike’: Russian Lawmaker Calls for Nuclear Strike on Ukraine to Force Kyiv to Surrender — A senior Russian lawmaker has openly called for Moscow to use tactical nuclear weapons against Ukraine to force Kyiv to surrender, dismissing debate over whether Russia should cross the nuclear threshold. His comments come amid fresh warnings about possible Russian escalation, though there is no evidence Putin has ordered an imminent nuclear strike.

Kremlin Says Putin Sees ‘Absolutely No Point’ in Trump-Zelensky Peace Summit — The Kremlin has dismissed the prospect of a Trump-Putin-Zelensky peace summit, saying there is “absolutely no point” in meeting without a deal ready to sign. The comments come after a reported secret CIA chief visit to Moscow and amid fresh warnings that Russia is preparing new offensives in northern Ukraine.

Ukraine’s Renaissance Legacy — Kyiv’s “Renaissance” mural symbolizes Ukraine’s rebirth, merging early Renaissance aesthetics with national resilience. Its imagery evokes dignity and self‑determination, connecting with Pico della Mirandola’s humanist ideals and the will demonstrated so strongly by Ukrainians to have the right to determine their own future in the face of aggression.

Ukraine and Israel Draw Closer as Israeli Elections Loom — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described Iran as a common threat in an Independence Day letter to President Volodymyr Zelensky, following renewed high-level contact in Washington in July. The outreach marks an improvement after years of restrained Israeli support and a sharp dispute over grain from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories, although major policy decisions are unlikely before Israel’s next government is formed.

Can Ukraine Set a New Standard in International Law? — International law can punish attacks on cultural sites but struggles to account for long-term harm to memory, language, education and identity. After more than 12 years of Russian occupation, Ukraine has a unique body of evidence with which to argue that the cultural dimension of genocide must be addressed not only academically, but legally.

UK Ukrainian Church Leader on Faith, Diaspora & 35 Years of Independence — Protopresbyter Bohdan Matwijczuk, Dean of the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church in Great Britain, was in Kyiv for the celebrations of the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s modern independence. He tells Kyiv Post about the Ukrainian community in the UK, his role as one of its spiritual leaders, and their enduring tight bond with Ukraine.

A Ukrainian Who Stood Up to War Criminal Ratko Mladić — Bosnian Serb commander Ratko Mladić died while serving a life sentence for genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes. His death recalls the little-known mission of Ukrainian Col. Mykola Verkhohliad, who negotiated an evacuation from Žepa under armed pressure, insisted that families not be separated, and placed peacekeepers aboard the buses carrying civilians to safety.

Iceland Voters Reject Resuming EU Membership Talks in Referendum — Iceland voters have rejected a government-backed referendum to reopen European Union membership talks, broadcaster RUV reported on Sunday, Aug. 30. The “no” campaign successfully argued that joining the EU would jeopardize the island’s sovereignty and vital fishing waters, countering arguments that membership would ease high interest rates and improve regional security. How Russia’s Cultural Projects Conceal Their Human Atrocities — Russia continues to use culture and internationally recognized artists to advance its influence abroad and promote the normalization of relations with Moscow despite the ongoing war. Russian violinists Vadim Repin and Mikhail Simonyan are examples of Kremlin-linked cultural engagement that, ultimately, cannot be separated from Russia’s actions in Ukraine.

UK Defense Bosses Warned of Russian Spy Threats Amid Escalation — Executives of British defense firms supplying weapons to Ukraine have been warned about the risk of being targeted by Russian spies, following a summer roundtable organized by the FCDO. The warning comes amid the disruption of Russian assassination plots against European defense figures, including the CEO of Germany’s Rheinmetall.

Blowtorch and Keyboard Can Also Be Weapons of Victory — Not every potential military serviceperson is suited to serving on the front line with a weapon in hand. Especially now, as robots take over, the skill sets needed are much broader. Recruiters are taking that into account.

Katheryn Winnick in Kyiv: On War, UNITED24, Ukrainian Roots and Favorite Dish — Actress and United24 platform ambassador Katheryn Winnick shares with Kyiv Post her impressions from her third visit to wartime Kyiv, nights under missile and drone attacks, and the work of the Winnick Foundation. She discusses combating global “war fatigue,” supporting Ukrainian children and women, why it’s important to encourage Hollywood film-making about Ukrainian history, and why she dreams of portraying Queen O

Moscow Sentences Ex-Ukrainian Adviser Arestovych to 11 Years in Prison — A judge at Moscow’s Second Western District Military Court has sentenced Oleksiy Arestovych, a former adviser to the Ukrainian president’s office, to 11 years in prison in absentia. The court found him guilty of spreading “false information” regarding the April 2022 Russian missile strike on Kramatorsk and calling for terrorism by urging railway sabotage. Arestovych, who resigned from his advisory role in January 2023 and n

Ukraine Reaches Winter Gas Reserve Target of 14.6B Cubic Meters Early — Ukraine has reached its target of 14.6 billion cubic meters of natural gas reserves a month ahead of schedule, ensuring baseline coverage for the 2026-2027 winter season. The early accumulation comes as the government pushes to decentralize the energy grid and protect infrastructure from anticipated Russian attacks.

Khmara Details Plan to Close $27B Defense Deficit, Appoints New Team — Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara has outlined strategies to resolve a $27 billion defense funding deficit by advancing European loans and engaging new international partners. Speaking to journalists, Khmara emphasized institutional continuity within the ministry, revealing new leadership appointments for frontline operations, human capital, and international partnerships. Khmara also confirmed he had reached out to his predeces

Belgium Rejects Renewed EU Push to Fund Ukraine With Frozen Assets — Belgian Defense Minister Theo Francken stated that utilizing €200 billion ($232 billion) in immobilized Russian assets to support Ukraine remains “non-negotiable,” pushing back against a renewed effort by Sweden, Poland, the Netherlands, and Spain. Speaking on television, Francken warned Baltic nations against cornering Belgium over the issue, given the assets are largely held at the Belgian clearinghouse Euroclear.

EU Prepares New Sanctions Package Targeting 1,600 Russian Entities — The EU is drafting an expanded sanctions package against Russia that could target up to 1,600 individuals and legal entities, according to European diplomats. The proposal, which evenly targets 800 people and 800 organizations, will be discussed at the EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Ireland next week, with an expected adoption date in mid-October.

Missile Strike on Kharkiv Memorial Run Leaves 3 Dead — A Russian ballistic missile, preliminarily identified as an Iskander-M, struck the village of Natalyne in the Kharkiv region on the morning of Aug. 29 during an annual memorial run for fallen soldiers. The attack killed three people, including a local police officer, and injured two others. The incident prompted local prosecutors to launch a criminal investigation into official negligence against the event’s organizers for failing to ensure

Russian Strikes Hit Odesa Food Hub, Kill 1 in Zaporizhzhia Drone Attack — A series of Russian drone and aerial attacks across southern and southeastern Ukraine on Saturday evening and early Sunday morning killed at least one civilian and injured ten others. In the Zaporizhzhia region, FPV drones and guided bombs killed a 73-year-old woman and injured five others across multiple settlements. In Odesa, an overnight strike targeted a civilian food storage warehouse, sparking a massive fire and inju

Ukraine Strikes Russian Radar, Command Posts, and Pantsir-S1 System — The Ukrainian Defense Forces struck multiple Russian military targets on Aug. 29, including a radar station in Russia’s Bryansk region, command posts in the Luhansk region, and drone facilities in the Donetsk region. The military also targeted logistics warehouses in occupied Crimea and the Donetsk region, alongside an ammunition depot in Kadiivka. Additionally, the General Staff confirmed the destruction of a Russian Pantsir-

Ukrainian Media Over 35 Years of Independence. Part IV. Anna Babinets on Investigations and the Secrets of Ukrainian Officials — Four well-known Ukrainian journalists from different areas of the media industry – television (Oksana Sokolova), business journalism (Dmytro Koshovyi), investigative journalism (Anna Babinets), and regional and online media (Serhii Nikitenko) – tell the story of journalism in Ukraine.

Finnish President Stubb Dismisses Imminent Russian Threat to NATO — Finnish President Alexander Stubb said that he does not believe Russia will attack NATO territory, contradicting recent warnings from the German Defense Ministry regarding a potential conflict by 2029. Stubb cited NATO’s overwhelming conventional and nuclear deterrence, along with severe Russian troop depletion in Ukraine.
British Defence Intelligence Update Ukraine Aug. 26, 2026 — British Defence Intelligence.

Russia Vows Major Strikes on Ukrainian Energy Grid — The Russian Ministry of Defense announced on Sunday, Aug. 30, that it is preparing “massive strikes” against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. The ministry justified the planned attacks as retaliation for Ukraine’s ongoing drone campaign against Russian oil refineries and commercial logistics facilities.

Russia Extends Fuel Export Ban Amid Record Refinery Strikes — The Russian government has extended its ban on diesel and marine fuel exports by producers until Sept. 30 in an effort to stabilize the domestic market. The extension follows a record 21 Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in August, driving refining capacity to its lowest level in over two decades. August refining averaged just 3.8 million barrels per day, causing a 20% drop in gasoline supplies and a 23% drop in diesel

Death Toll in Myla Ammunition Depot Blast Reaches 38 — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Aug. 30, that the death toll from a Russian drone strike on an ammunition warehouse in the village of Myla (Bucha district, Kyiv region) has reached 38 people. Twenty people were injured, including two children, and four remain missing following the Friday night blast, which triggered massive secondary detonations. Zelensky noted that State Emergency Service pyrotechnic units are working arou

Ukraine’s Scientific Independence — Ukraine's scientific independence in 1991 was built on a rich Soviet-era legacy rather than starting from scratch, producing figures such as welding pioneer Borys Paton and Fields Medal winner Maryna Viazovska. Since then, the country has developed strengths in materials science, pharmaceuticals and radiation-detection technology, while deepening ties with European research networks. Despite severe damage from Russia's full-scale invasion, Ukraine's scientific

Germany to Blame Russia for Leipzig Drone Attack, Plan Sanctions — The German government is preparing to officially blame Russia for the Aug. 4 explosive drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport and impose broad sanctions. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is expected to announce the measures early next week, potentially aligning with new EU sanctions. Berlin reportedly considers standard diplomatic expulsions insufficient and is exploring tougher penalties, including increased military aid to Ukraine.

Car Bomb Targets Olenivka Prison Official in Occupied Donetsk — On the night of Aug. 29, a car bombing in temporarily occupied Donetsk targeted Dmytro Neielov, the first deputy head of the Olenivka penal colony. Neielov is accused of torturing and humiliating Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilians, and his current condition is unknown. In the spring of 2026, Ukrainian authorities charged Neielov in absentia with war crimes. The Olenivka colony is notorious for a July 2022 explosion that killed

Drones Strike Yeysk Airfield and Major Kirishi Oil Refinery in Russia — Early Sunday morning, Aug. 30, Ukrainian drones struck a military airfield in Yeysk, Krasnodar Krai, and the KINEF oil refinery in the Leningrad region. Satellite data and local reports indicated fires and secondary detonations at the Yeysk airfield. In the Leningrad region, Governor Alexander Drozdenko claimed 42 drones were intercepted but confirmed a fire at the Kirishi industrial zone. The KINEF refinery is one of Russia

Ukrainian Perception of Poland Plummets to 50% — A Rating Group survey conducted between August 4 and 9 found that only 50% of Ukrainians now consider Poland a friendly country, a sharp decline from 79% in February 2024 and 94% in 2023. The poll also revealed differing views on Polish leadership, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk viewed positively by 45% of respondents, while President Karol Nawrocki received a 62% negative rating. Meanwhile, France, the UK, and Germany topped the list of nations

CIA Chief Proposed Trump-Putin-Zelensky Summit — CIA Director John Ratcliffe proposed a trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, President Volodymyr Zelensky, and Russian President Vladimir Putin during his unannounced visit to Moscow. Ratcliffe met with SVR head Sergei Naryshkin and FSB Director Alexander Bortnikov, viewing the latter as a “constructive player” who might persuade Putin to resume US-mediated talks.

Russian Drone Strikes on Kyiv Spark Fires, Injure 3 — Russian forces launched another massive drone attack on Kyiv on the evening of Aug. 29, injuring at least three people and sparking fires across four districts, according to the State Emergency Service. A strike in the Obolon district hit a 12-story residential building, while other fires were reported in the Podil, Holosiiv, and Desna districts. The evening barrage marked the third consecutive day of strikes on the capital.
